text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The newspaper publishes a report on billiard clubs opened in post-communist Romania. In 1995 alone, Romania imported accessories worth $4.4 million.
- One in three Romanians in work had been involved in a labour conflict over the past six years, the newspaper says in a report.
- The State Ownership Fund (FPS) is to change conditions for privatisation through selling shares to company employees.
- The newspaper publishes a two-page report in hard currency exchange regulations in Romania and other East European countries.
- Demand for office space indicates the changes following November 1996 elections. In 1996, there was a demand for 28,000 square metres while this year it is for 40,000 square metres.
BURSA
- Gabrile Mihut, FPS manager, gives an interview on difficulties and successes in privatisation.
- Banca Comerciala Romana concluded a credit accord worth $7.5 million with U.S. Exim BANK to support the restructuring of the Sidex Galati steel plant.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- International Hotel began the construction of a 30-storey hotel with 300 rooms close to the Romanian state television.
- Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said the 1997 state budget would be revised in early August.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The upper house, the Senate, adopted the bill to reorganise the state-run regie autonomes.
- More than half of Romania's 162,000 farming implements are over eight years old.
ADEVARUL

- George Constantin Paunescu, head of extensive local tourism and trade businesses, investigated by prosecuotrs over allegations he illegally obtained a stake in a commercial bank, was hospitalised with heart trouble.
- The central bank hopes the overliquidity on the interbank market will be soaked up by a big harvest.
General
All newspapers report on the explosion of a Romanian-made bomb during tests in the southern town of Craiova, which killed 16 people and injured two.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Leaders of all parliamentary parties comment on the decision taken by NATO member states to leave Romania out of the first wave of enlargement but to consider it a prime candidate for subsequent waves.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Bucharest's mayor wants to offer visiting U.S. President Bill Clinton the keys to the city, an icon and a bottle of vintage wine.
ADEVARUL
- Economic reform is the real test which Romania has to pass after the Madrid summit, says an editorial.
- The newspaper publishes a report on the situation of high-school graduates in Romania, who make half of the country's unemployed.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
